answer: **Yes.** The passage balances the two well. The real-time scene carries the narrative: Gregor wakes, looks at his body, thinks aloud ("Was ist mit mir geschehen?"), and tries again and again to roll onto his right side. Exposition is woven in sparingly and serves the scene, such as the brief note that "Samsa war Reisender," the fabric samples, and the history of the framed picture. Even the compressed moment ("Er versuchte es wohl hundertmal") stays tied to the immediate action. Neither mode dominates, so the opening is vivid while still giving the reader the background they need.
